text:
Situation: Carboplatin has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2023-04-28 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale Lakeside holds critically low stock (1.5–2.5 days on hand). Corvale East holds 54 units of the 60 mL vial (15.1 days) and 77 units of the 5 mL vial (20.6 days). Corvale General holds three lots totaling roughly 76 units (9 days each).

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the carboplatin shortage on 2023-04-28. The Accord Healthcare product listed uses carboplatin manufactured by Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited. FDA inspection 1191818 at Intas ended 2022-12-02 and was classified OAI; the classification letter is dated 2023-04-05, 23 days before the shortage posting. FDA subsequently issued an import alert for Intas on 2023-06-01 and a warning letter on 2023-07-28. An alternate manufacturer, Apotex Corp., is approved for same-product substitution; its plant Teyro Labs Private Limited received a VAI classification on 2025-11-12.

Our position: Lakeside inventory is insufficient to support upcoming regimens. East can spare supply while retaining a two-week buffer. Apotex product is approved for substitution and available.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 26 units of carboplatin 10 mg/mL 60 mL vial from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside. Approval: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 2 units of carboplatin 10 mg/mL 5 mL vial from Corvale East to Corvale General. Approval: Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
3. Activate same-product substitution to Apotex Corp. carboplatin 10 mg/mL. Approval: Pharmacist (substitution per Alex Morgan, PharmD approval 2026-05-16).
4. Prepare Teva Parenteral Medicines carboplatin 10 mg/mL as alternate concentration/vial size if needed. Approval: Pharmacist (verification per Casey Nguyen, MD approval 2026-01-18).

Not recommended: Delay transfers pending new purchase orders; rely solely on General campus stock to cover Lakeside; initiate compounding or dose-rounding protocols without P&T review.
